evidence_bar_now_met_but_deliberately_no: The register requires two independent observations, or one plus an observed standalone pass. Both are now satisfied. It is still NOT entered as a register entry, for two reasons that outlast this slice. First, a register entry is a licence to attribute a red run, and this failure should never be attributed: unlike the three entries just closed, nobody has established that it is load sensitivity rather than a real defect in the propagation path it exercises. Second, its surface necessarily includes apps/web/**, so every UI slice - Slice B included - would lose the attribution anyway, leaving an entry that grants nothing and never closes. That is the defect the register's own closing rule warns about.
why_it_was_not_repaired_by_phase11_brows: Decision D1 at that slice's activation, resolved on evidence at its stage-1 gate. The file imports chromium from @playwright/test and expect from vitest, so Playwright's web-first assertions are unavailable in it and locator.waitFor is already the strongest primitive it has. Its proof is that a real simulator-to-edge-to-server-to-poll pipeline propagates a count, with no signal to await but the text itself, and page.clock cannot substitute because effectiveFreshness compares page time against real server timestamps. Making that arrival deterministic requires mocking the pipeline, which deletes the assertion's end-to-end meaning — the one thing that slice's constraint forbade.
what_the_contention_slice_adds: It rules out the cheap fix in advance. The eight hardcoded locator.waitFor({ timeout: 5_000 }) calls at :739, :769, :773, :779, :783, :788, :792 and :797 sit inside a test that already carries an explicit timeout: 60_000 at :628, so no vitest test-level budget is what expires. And raising a waiting budget was directly tested on the sibling browser class and falsified: assertions given 20000ms still failed with the element absent. Anyone reaching for a larger timeout here should read docs/phase-records/verification/20260823-p11_ladder_contention_b01-falsification-result.json first.
what_a_real_repair_would_have_to_do: Either establish, with evidence, that the failure is load sensitivity and not a genuine propagation defect — which needs the observed tail-latency distribution of the simulator-to-render path under ladder load, not another timeout guess — or find a signal in that pipeline that can be awaited deterministically without mocking any part of what the test exists to prove. Neither fits inside a slice scoped to assertion sampling.
